subject: POC trial planning: success criteria & KPIs (Atlas Payments)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning: success criteria & KPIs (Atlas Payments)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have a shared set of success criteria and next steps for the POC/trial.

Goal:
- Validate Redwood Inference as the production inference layer for Atlas Payments’ fraud-classification and enrichment flows (real-time inference in payments path and async enrichment batch).

Proposed success criteria / KPIs (initial):
- Latency: p95 inference latency < 200 ms (target) for 512-token context; p50 < 100 ms.
- Throughput: sustain 100 req/s for the real-time path with <1% tail queueing; burst capacity to 300 req/s.
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0006 (post-quantization config).
- Quality: intent/label accuracy >= 95% on your labeled test set; hallucination rate < 2% measured by sampling + human review.
- Reliability: 99.9% availability during test window; graceful fallback to smaller model when capacity constrained.

Evaluation plan:
- You’ll provide a 10k-example evaluation set (anonymized) and baseline model outputs. Redwood will run an A/B of baseline vs. candidate model used in the trial.
- Metrics: per-request latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), tokens-per-request, cost per token, top-1 accuracy, precision/recall for fraud labels, and human-eval notes for hallucinations.
- Acceptance: KPIs above must be met on the majority of traffic patterns and on the evaluation set.

Timeline & ownership (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize test data and access — OWNER: Alex (Atlas) + Marissa (Redwood).
- Week 1: Redwood infra + test harness ready; baseline runs — OWNER: Lauren (test harness), Rishi (infra).
- Week 2: Live pilot with shadow traffic and monitored comparisons; finalize go/no-go — OWNER: Jordan/Marissa.

Next steps:
1) Alex — confirm availability of the anonymized eval set and whether you prefer synthetic masking or a direct S3 share.
2) Atlas — confirm desired start date for the 2-week trial (we suggested starting small and scaling).
3) Redwood team — attach trial metrics template and POC MOP (see attachments).

Attachments: trial-metrics-template.xlsx (template for results), redwood-poc-mop.pdf (operational playbook)
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ATL-5423

Happy to hop on a quick 30-min kickoff if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]
[Attachment: trial-metrics-template.xlsx]

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@atlaspayments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC trial planning: success criteria & KPIs (Atlas Payments)

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear recap. High level we’re aligned on the approach. A few notes from our side:

- Latency: our current infra puts some requests through an edge hop; realistic p95 target for our production topology would be ~250 ms. Can we set p95 <= 250 ms as the acceptance target but keep the 200 ms goal for standalone benchmarks?
- Throughput: we’d like to validate up to 200 req/s as a breakpoint for our peak windows; happy to run an initial 100 req/s steady-state and spike tests to 200 req/s.
- Cost: target cost/token looks reasonable; please also report end-to-end cost including any gateway overhead.
- Quality: when you say "human-eval notes for hallucinations" — can you define the sampling plan (sample size, strata)? We prefer stratified sampling across high-risk transactions.

We can provide an anonymized 12k-row evaluation set; I’ll confirm the exact S3 share by EOD Friday. Also attaching our security questionnaire — Marissa, Rishi, would you please review?

Proposed kickoff: start trial week of July 12 (gives us time to review security bits). If Redwood can do an earlier starting window we can consider July 7 but need internal signoff.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Director, Machine Learning Engineering | Atlas Payments
[Attachment: atlas-security-questionnaire.pdf]

Subject: Re: POC trial planning: success criteria & KPIs (Atlas Payments)

Alex —

Thanks for the notes — totally reasonable. Proposed adjustments (so we capture both the real-world constraint and a stretch target):

- Latency: p95 <= 250 ms (acceptance on production topology). Additionally track standalone bench p95 <= 200 ms for kernel-level optimization. p50 target <= 120 ms.
- Throughput: steady-state baseline 100 req/s, run spike tests to 200 req/s; measure queueing and tail latency.
- Cost: aim for <= $0.00055/token as the delivery target; report end-to-end.
- Quality: sampling plan — 200 stratified samples/week across high/medium/low risk buckets, plus automated diff vs. baseline for the full 12k eval set. Human review on any outputs with > 10% confidence-delta.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Alex (Atlas) — confirm S3 share and masking approach by Fri 07/02.
- Lauren (Redwood) — deliver test harness + synthetic traffic scripts by Tue 07/06.
- Rishi (Redwood infra) — provision dedicated trial pool + monitoring by Tue 07/06.
- Marissa (Redwood CS) — schedule kickoff and coordinate access, target Wed 07/07 for a 30-min sync.

I’ve updated the trial metrics template to reflect the adjusted latency/cost rows (attached). Once we have the S3 share I’ll run an initial baseline and post results to the Drive link.

If that all looks good I’ll block the Wed 07/07 10:00 AM PT kickoff (30 minutes) and loop in the infra/observability leads.

Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: trial-metrics-template.xlsx]
